subject: Re: Encryption & KMS options — follow up from demo
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Jenkins <alice.jenkins@acme-fin.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Encryption & KMS options — follow up from demo

Hi Alice / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great discussion. As promised, a short recap of what we covered and the immediate next steps so your security/procurement teams have what they need: 

1) Summary of questions you raised:
   - Customer-managed keys (CMEK) / HSM-backed keys requirement
   - In-transit vs at-rest encryption details and certificate management
   - Logging and audit trails (PII redaction, retention windows)
   - Data residency (US-East preferred)

2) What Redwood can provide today (high level):
   - In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers by default; mTLS available for Dedicated/Private installs.
   - At-rest: All customer data is encrypted at-rest. For Hosted API we offer envelope encryption where data keys (CEKs) are wrapped by KMS keys.
   - CMEK: We support AWS KMS & GCP KMS CMEK integration for Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API supports CMEK for some enterprise customers (let's confirm for your specific procurement model).
   - HSM: HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3) are supported in Private deployments; for Hosted, we use cloud-provider HSM-backed KMS (AWS KMS) but do not support customer-imported HSM modules in the shared hosted tier.
   - Logs & retention: Access logs and operator audit logs available. We can configure event logging to avoid storing full user payloads and provide redaction flags. Retention windows are configurable via contract.

Attached: Redwood_Security_Overview.pdf, CMEK_Integration_Guide.pdf, SOC2_Type2_Report.pdf

Next steps I propose:
 - Please confirm whether your procurement requires keys to be non-exportable and HSM-import (i.e., do you need to import your own HSM keys or is AWS/GCP-managed HSM sufficient?).
 - If you require an HSM-import option, we should plan a technical session with our infra/crypto engineers (cc'ing Jordan and Dev).
 - Let me know your desired retention window for logs and any specific PII redaction requirements.

Once I have your answers I'll set up a 30-45 minute follow-up with our engineering/security leads.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0193

Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS options — follow up from demo

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the summary — that aligns with our notes. A few clarifications from the security team: 

- Key management: Acme requires customer-managed keys with HSM backing. Specifically, keys must be customer-controlled and non-exportable. We can use AWS KMS as long as keys are in our account and HSM-backed (no exporting).
- Key rotation: We require support for key rotation and automation for re-wrapping CEKs.
- Logging: Audit logs must not contain raw PII. We need confirmation that request/response payloads will not be stored in plaintext in logs and that you can guarantee configurable retention (7 years is our default for financial audits).
- Data residency: All production data must remain in the US-East region.

Also please confirm whether your hosted offering supports our procurement requirement of keys in our AWS account (KMS keys in Acme's account) or if the CMEK option is limited to Dedicated/Private.

If you can send the SOC2 and integration guide that will help our InfoSec kickoff the procurement packet.

Best,
Alice Jenkins
Head of Security, Acme Financial
alice.jenkins@acme-fin.com | +1 (212) 555-0148

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS options — follow up from demo

Hi Alice,

Thanks for the clear list — good to have those constraints upfront. Quick answers while I loop in engineering for any fine-grained technical confirmations: 

- Customer KMS in your account: Yes, we support using customer-owned KMS keys (keys in the customer's AWS/GCP project) for wrapping CEKs. For Hosted API customers we have a CMEK path that allows you to provide an AWS KMS key in your account; usage is implemented via IAM-granted encrypt/decrypt/GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext calls so the plaintext key material never leaves the KMS.

- Non-exportable / HSM: If you have AWS KMS keys that are HSM-backed (AWS KMS with AWS CloudHSM), those keys are non-exportable and meet the HSM-backed requirement. If you need to import your own HSM tokens (BYO-HSM), that is currently supported in Private deployments — we will need to validate the import path and attestations with our infra team.

- Key rotation: Supported — we rotate CEKs and can trigger re-wraps via KMS. You retain control over the master key lifecycle in your account.

- Logging & PII: Our hosted ingestion pipeline does not persist raw request/response payloads to long-term operator logs by default. We can provide access logs that record metadata (timestamps, model used, token counts, request IDs) and optional redaction for any recorded payloads. Retention windows are contract-configurable; seven-year retention for audit records is feasible for enterprise agreements.

- Data residency: We can pin service region to US-East for your tenant in Dedicated or Private. For Hosted, we have a US-East data region; we'll confirm the deployment footprint for your expected throughput.

Attaching the SOC2 report and the CMEK guide.

Next step: Jordan / Dev, can you confirm the Hosted CMEK implementation details and whether any limitations apply for high-throughput workloads? Also please flag any items that would require a Private deployment to satisfy Acme's BYO-HSM requirement.

Alice / Tom, would a technical session with our infra/security engineers early next week work? I'm available Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Encryption & KMS options — internal confirmation

Marissa / team — internal summary for the record and for sharing in the technical session: 

1) Hosted CMEK implementation (current):
   - We support customer KMS keys (AWS/GCP) for CEK wrapping via API gateway -> key-access layer. The service performs GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext and stores only the encrypted CEK (no plaintext storage).
   - For AWS customers, we require an IAM role/grant from the customer's account. We can use KMS Grants to reduce cross-account permission footprint for high throughput.
   - HSM-backed keys (AWS KMS backed by AWS CloudHSM) are supported and are non-exportable. This satisfies 'non-exportable HSM' requirements without requiring key import.

2) BYO-HSM / Import keys:
   - Importing key material into CloudHSM / third-party HSM and connecting that into our runtime is supported only in Private deployments today. The hosted multi-tenant environment cannot accept imported key material from customer HSMs due to tenancy/isolation concerns.
   - For a Private deployment, we'll need to validate the HSM vendor, key wrapping algorithms, and provide an import runbook. This typically adds ~2-4 weeks of engineering/provisioning work plus compliance attestations.

3) Logging & PII:
   - By default we do not log full request/response payloads to operator logs. We keep request/response hashes and metadata for debugging.
   - We can enable payload logging for debugging with PII redaction hooks in the ingestion pipeline. Redaction rules are configurable; however, we need to validate patterns with Acme's InfoSec to ensure coverage.
   - Retention: We support configurable retention for audit logs; 7-year retention will require archival configuration and potentially additional storage costs (to be captured in commercial terms).

4) Performance / high throughput notes:
   - Using cross-account KMS introduces a small per-request latency (KMS generate/decrypt calls). We mitigate this with encrypted CEK caching and batching; for customers with very high QPS we recommend Dedicated pools pinned to the same region as the KMS to minimize latency.

Action items:
 - I'll prepare a short slide (tech one-pager) showing hosted CMEK flow, the non-exportable HSM option via AWS KMS, and the Private BYO-HSM path.
 - Proposed timeline: 2 weeks to prepare PoC materials and schedule a customer-facing technical session. If Acme requires BYO-HSM/Private, add 2-4 weeks for provisioning.

Let me know if I should include any additional diagrams or a sample policy document for the KMS IAM role.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
